chapter: Pay, the Fletcher Henderson circle and later life
title: Hawkins's criticism of Russell Smith's lead playing
summary: Dance says Hawkins faulted Russell Smith's lead trumpet and Fletcher's loss of Cootie Williams; Caldwell notes Hawk seldom criticized.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: You know, Hawk didn't like Russell those.
No, I don't know what happened with them. They -- somehow they didn't --

Well, I -- I mean apart from any more than once personal thing, he said -- he told me I never could forgive Fletcher for letting Cootie Williams go, and he didn't -- I mean nearly everybody says -- nearly everybody says what a great lead Russell Smith was. But Hawkins didn't liked that lead. I think he thought that, you know, that was precise and everything, but that didn't -- that didn't sort of get enough sort of punch out of that trumpet section. I don't -- I never (unintelligible), but he told me that more than once. One of the with few musicians he would sort of -- you know, he criticized like that.
Hawk was that way. He (never) criticized anybody criticized anybody very seldom because (unintelligible).
You know, he doesn't come out. That must have been -- or maybe there was another reason.
But he was quite definite about that.
